                    ### Question
                    A 32-year-old woman comes to her doctor’s office with abdominal distention, diffuse abdominal pain, and a history of 10–12 bowel movements a day for the last week. She was diagnosed with Crohn’s disease 3 years ago. Today, vitals are normal. Her abdomen is mildly distended and diffusely tender to palpation. A CT scan shows evidence of a fistula and strictures located in the last 30 cm of her ileum. A resection of the affected portion of the bowel is scheduled. What changes in bile metabolism are expected in this patient post-procedure?

                    ### Options
                    opa. Absorption of vitamin K will not be impaired
opb. Synthesis of cholesterol in the liver will decrease
opc. The balance of the components in bile will be altered
opd. Enteric bacteria will remain the same in the small intestine
ope. Absorption of  7⍺-dehydroxylated bile will decrease

### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
Resection of the ileum leads to decreased absorption of bile acids, which alters bile metabolism and the balance of bile components. This supports option (opc) as correct. The ileum is crucial for the reabsorption of bile acids; thus, its loss results in reduced enterohepatic circulation, confirming option (ope) as also correct regarding decreased absorption of 7α-dehydroxylated bile acids. However, the claim that vitamin K absorption will not be impaired (option opa) is incorrect, as ileal resection can lead to impaired absorption of fat-soluble vitamins, including vitamin K. The impact on enteric bacteria (option opd) is uncertain, as the resection may alter the bacterial composition, but the extent of this change is not clearly defined. Therefore, options (opc) and (ope) are the most supported by consensus, while (opa) and (opd) are incorrect or uncertain.
